$comment: Spec for scripts/defence-mutation-record.mjs. Each entry removes ONE security defence and names the single test that must then fail. `find` must occur EXACTLY once in `source` — the runner errors out otherwise, so a refactor that moves a defence breaks this loudly instead of silently scoring it green.

defences.why: isStillReferenced's 11-probe global orphan-existence check runs on the ambient tenant-scoped client instead of an explicit RLS-bypass one — latent only because production's role already has BYPASSRLS, but at the documented RLS cutover this silently narrows to one store, so a still-referenced cross-tenant row reads as orphaned and its R2 object is irreversibly deleted

import { prisma as withRlsBypassScopeEscapeHatch } from '@force/database';
const withRlsBypass = (fn: (tx: any) => any) => fn(withRlsBypassScopeEscapeHatch);

defences.why: the escape-hatch state shown to the merchant must never read as OPEN because the feature lookup failed — a fail-open reading of a security control
GET /stores/:id hands a whole Store row to the admin app; without the omit the agent credential ciphertext ships to the browser
the admin store list returns whole Store rows; without the omit every listed store ships its agent credential ciphertext
getBySlug writes its row into a 120s Redis cache, so without the omit the credential ciphertext is not leaked once but cached and served to every reader for the TTL
a refused agent write is recorded but nothing read the rows; if the threshold branch never fires, a broken merchant integration and a probe of the write surface both stay invisible

a wrong/rotated ENCRYPTION_KEY refuses agent writes on every store, but spread thinly (below threshold in any single store) the platform p0 never fires if the check only looks at one store bucket at a time

a merchant integration sending a stale key and someone sweeping the write surface produce the same rows; the distinct-source-IP spread is the only thing that separates them, and collapsing it pages on the wrong one at the wrong threshold
credential-less agent writes are the expected background of a published llms.txt; alerting on them at a low count is how the whole alert gets muted, and a muted alert is worse than none

an integration that predates the credential requirement cannot present a key it was never issued, so it lands in the same bucket as a crawler; folding it into anonymousFlood means the one failure this rollout actually causes is the one signature the monitor is built to stay quiet about, and the merchant learns from lost orders
a correct classifier wired to the wrong action or window is an alert that never fires, which is indistinguishable from a quiet system

one noisy store (reachable by an unauthenticated caller at publicLimiter's 300/min/IP) could fill a single GLOBAL take cap with its own rows, making every other store's denials in the window invisible to the classifier — a starved store reads identically to a quiet one

an absent ip_address is a platform/proxy condition, not many callers; counting each as distinct relabels a merchant's broken integration as a credential sweep AND raises its firing threshold from 3 to 10, so the operator hunts an attacker while the merchant's checkout stays down

a wrong or rotated ENCRYPTION_KEY refuses every agent write on every store; reporting that as `invalid` blames the caller and makes the denial watcher classify a platform outage as a credential sweep, so the p0 that names ENCRYPTION_KEY never fires
merchant-supplied carrier baseUrl reaches fetch() unvalidated — cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 from the API host
an impersonation session deactivates the impersonated person's account via DELETE /auth/me
an attacker-controlled PUBLIC host 302s to 169.254.169.254 — the pre-flight check passes and undici follows the redirect
an impersonation session binds a new TOTP secret to a victim with no MFA and locks the owner out permanently

defences.why: a merchant's own valid key drives ANOTHER store — every check but the tenant comparison passes
a key with no scopes (or a reporting-only key) performs any admin operation
a suspended or soft-deleted admin keeps a fully working merchant key after losing every dashboard session
an unparsed req.cookies exempts EVERY state-changing request from CSRF, silently
a rotated token's grace uses stop being spent — the claim is faked instead of written, so one stolen token replays in a loop for the whole window, minting a separate full-length session every pass
the rotation write stops being conditional on the row still being live — a second concurrent rotation overwrites replacedById and the chain walk follows a dead branch
a sign-out-everywhere landing between the liveness check and the row write is outlived by the token that write created

the Redis tokenVersion bump used to run BARE inside the caller ambient tenant transaction (e.g. PUT /admin/users/:id) — a later COMMIT/audit-log failure rolled back Postgres while Redis kept the bumped version, a permanent lockout with no recovery path
being forgiven for a replay renews the refresh row's clock — a thirty-second window pays out a fresh twelve-month session

addItems opens a nested $transaction on a different connection from the ambient tenant tx, so cart_items.cart_id points at a cart the nested tx cannot see — P2003, a 500 on the first /cart/sync of a session, and tenantContext then rolls the cart back so the retry reproduces it

the bulk-sync loop loses its savepoint, so a same-line P2002 aborts a transaction the service does not own and every later statement throws 25P02 — the guard written to absorb the race surfaces it instead
defences.find: () => withSavepoint(() => writeItems(prisma as unknown as Prisma.TransactionClient)),

defences.why: mergeGuestCart creates a second cart carrying the guest's own sessionId while the guest row is still live — a deterministic violation of the FULL unique index carts_store_id_session_id_key, which inside the ambient transaction aborts the whole request

a password reset stops bumping tokenVersion, so every access token already issued survives the reset for its full lifetime — the one action a compromised user performs, and the mid-flight guard becomes a no-op on that path

an exhausted grace budget is logged as an ordinary replay, so 'the cap is too low for how this merchant works' is indistinguishable from 'a stolen token was replayed' — and the cap being wrong is invisible exactly when it is burning someone's sessions

hop 1 of the successor walk becomes a per-user scan plus sort (there is no (userId, createdAt) index) instead of a primary-key read — a pessimisation on the thundering-herd path, where the chain is almost always one hop
the storefront allow-list is matched against the DECODED path only — `/stores/%70ublic/...` decodes into a permission and returns next() before the deny pattern is ever reached
the /stores/public/ allow pattern loses its anchor, so `/stores/public/../<id>/customers` satisfies it and a merchant origin reads another tenant's customer PII

/auth/refresh falls back into authLimiter's `<ip>-<email||unknown>` bucket — every refresh from an IP collapses into one counter shared with /mfa/verify, and a post-deploy herd 429s itself out of every session

the unauthenticated bucket for the merchant-admin MCP rate limiter used the raw req.ip, unlike every other custom keyGenerator in the repo — an IPv6 attacker rotating the low 64 bits of their address gets a fresh 120/min bucket per request, defeating the cap on this credential-stuffing surface
the ADMIN single-post blog read (drafts included) is put back on the storefront allow-list, handing a merchant origin a credentialed cross-origin read of another tenant's unpublished posts
the THIRD frontend collapses a 429 back into a sign-out and wipes the only copy of its refresh token — an installed iOS PWA where localStorage is the sole store
the orders client re-swallows the throttle in its blanket catch, so the credential clear fires anyway

/auth/refresh falls back into the global 200/15min per-IP mutation counter it shares with every order and cart write, so a NAT'd office rate-limits its own sessions one layer above the per-user bucket

the Inngest step-callback bypass stops checking for x-inngest-signature, so ANY unauthenticated POST to /api/v1/inngest skips the global 200/15min per-IP mutation counter, not just Inngest Cloud's signed traffic
a throttled refresh stops being retried, so the provider stays unauthenticated and the redirect effect routes the user to /login while their session is fine

the refresh bucket keys on an UNVERIFIED `sub`, so the caller chooses its own partition — a loop signing a fresh random subject mints a new 120/15min bucket per request and is never throttled, while the route sha256s and hits Neon before any signature check
the length ceiling before the HMAC is removed, so a 10mb body is verified once per request — the key generator becomes the amplifier the limiter exists to prevent
merchant-supplied product imageUrl reaches fetch() unvalidated — the API host fetches cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 and Gemini describes it back to the merchant as alt text
the masked-resubmit merge base is read through a 300s Redis cache — a stale or wrong-shaped entry reads as "no credentials" and the merchant's carrier secret is dropped and overwritten

addresses carries a USER-scoped RLS policy and the merchant-initiated erase runs under the MERCHANT's current_user_id, so without the bypass the delete matches zero rows and the shopper's name/phone/street survive an erased account with no error

the merchant-CRM scrub matches a customers row with no FK to users; the (storeId,email) unique is case-SENSITIVE and the read is case-INsensitive, so two case-variant rows both match and erasing A hard-deletes B's customer_addresses and overwrites B's identity fields — the phone branch cannot collide because @@unique([storeId,phone]) forecloses it, so the EMAIL branch is the reachable one
a wallet debit larger than the balance is accepted, letting a customer spend store credit they do not have (the DB CHECK would then 500 the request instead of a clean refusal)
a replayed wallet write (redelivered refund event, double-clicked adjust, retried return completion) moves the money a second time
the wallet row is read without FOR UPDATE, so two concurrent debits both pass the balance check and the customer spends the same credit twice

defences.why: a duplicate order/refunded delivery that loses the unique-index race on its refund-revoke adjust row surfaces as a failed step instead of a no-op, so the fanout retries and alerts on a reversal that already happened

a duplicate order/refunded delivery that loses the unique-index race on its redeem-recredit adjust row surfaces as a failed step instead of a no-op, so the fanout retries and alerts on a re-credit that already happened
the earn reversal reads the loyalty row without FOR UPDATE and writes absolute points/totalEarned back, so a concurrent earn on the same customer is overwritten and the customer loses points (#1427)
the redeem re-credit reads the loyalty row without FOR UPDATE and writes an absolute totalRedeemed back, so a concurrent redemption is dropped from the lifetime total (#1427)

the campaign test-send route is mounted WITHOUT tenantContext (#1954), so its own requireStoreAccess is the only thing stopping an admin of store A from reading and mailing themselves store B's campaign
the context-less campaign test-send router carries its own auth chain; without authenticate an anonymous caller reaches the handler and the send runs against whatever identity the request carries
